entry.content:
PCDJ Reveals the Ultimate Mix of 2019’S Most Popular DJ Requested Songs (Top 200)

As they do each year, DJ Intelligence , a cloud-based event booking, planning, and management system for event professionals, has compiled a lists of client song requests made through their music request system at events around the world during 2019.

DJs are purveyors of music, and as is often the case for Mobile DJs, filling taking song requests from clients and patrons is part of the job.

DJ Intelligence offers a song request system as part of their platform, and they note the 2019 list of top requested songs was “Compiled by analyzing millions of song requests made through the DJ Intelligence music request system at weddings and parties around the world, this is the most accurate representation of what songs are being requested and played at live events.”

Whether or not you question the accuracy and how much the list of top requested songs deviates from your own experience, ‘millions’ of requests ain’t something to sneeze at.

There are are sizable number new songs on the 2019 chart that weren’t present on the previous years edition, but timeless event maintstay’s such as Mark Ronson & Bruno Mars’ “Uptown Funk” and Journey’s “Don’t Stop Believin’” are still chart-toppers.

While it’s 2019 and hot new tracks will make their way on to next years chart, the 2019 most requested list provide great insight for Mobile DJs. Make sure you have these tracks in your library. If you don’t subscribe to a record pool service, or you need songs released prior to two years ago you can try SoundCloud Go+ like many DEX 3 and DEX 3 RE DJs have. With 200+ million songs from popular artists and underground producers you’ll be able to fill every request.

2. In the Settings window, click on System.

3. On the left side of the window, click on Display. This will open up the display settings options.

4. You can adjust the brightness of your screen by using the slider located at the top of the page. You can also change the scaling of your screen by selecting one of the preset sizes or manually adjusting the slider.

5. To adjust the size of text and icons on your monitor, scroll down to the Scale and layout section. Here you can choose between the recommended size and manually entering a custom size. Once you have chosen the size you would like, click the Apply button to save your changes.

6. You can also adjust the orientation of your display by clicking the dropdown menu located under Orientation. You have the options to choose between landscape, portrait, and rotated.

7. Next, scroll down to the Multiple displays section. Here you can choose to extend your display or duplicate it onto another monitor.

8. Finally, scroll down to the Advanced display settings section. Here you can find more advanced display settings such as resolution and color depth.

By making these adjustments to your Windows 10 display settings, you can customize your desktop to fit your personal preference. Additionally, these settings can help improve the clarity of your monitor for a better viewing experience.
